commit_message:
[truetype] Fix Savannah bug #35601.

* src/truetype/ttinterp.c (Ins_SHZ): Use number of points instead of
last point for loop.
Also remove redundant boundary check.

findings.title: Out-of-bounds loop in Ins_SHZ due to unchecked contour-derived limit
findings.message: In Ins_SHZ, when the zone pointer gep2 is 1 (normal glyph zone), the loop limit is derived from `exc->zp2.contours[exc->zp2.n_contours - 1] + 1`. A maliciously crafted font can set the last contour end-index to a value exceeding the actual number of non-phantom points (n_points - 4), making `limit` larger than the valid range of `exc->zp2.cur` and `exc->zp2.tags` arrays. The subsequent loop `for (i = 0; i < limit; i++)` then calls `Move_Zp2_Point` with out-of-range indices, producing a heap buffer overflow. The original code that introduced this path (commit 96cddb8d) deliberately removed the previous bounds check (`BOUNDS(last_point, CUR.zp2.n_points)`) while also removing the +1 offset guard, leaving no validation that the contour-derived limit respects the actual array size.
findings.suggestion: Compute the loop limit using `n_points - 4U` for the normal zone (gep2 != 0), which correctly excludes the 4 phantom points appended by TrueType and is always bounded by the actual array size. Do not rely on values from the font's contours array to determine the iteration upper bound.

ground_truth.root_cause: When commit 96cddb8d replaced `last_point` (with a `BOUNDS` check) with an unchecked `limit` derived from `contours[n_contours - 1] + 1`, it removed the only guard that validated the font-supplied contour index against the actual point count. The contours array is font-controlled data and can contain arbitrary values; without a bounds check, the derived `limit` can freely exceed `n_points`, making the subsequent point-shifting loop iterate out of bounds.
